source: Yahoo Finance, read with the yfinance Python library (unofficial, not certified)

columns.prices.csv: date (exchange-local trading day), symbol (Yahoo), open/high/low/close (split-adjusted, not dividend-adjusted), adj_close (split- and dividend-adjusted: total return), volume, currency
columns.actions.csv: date (ex-date), symbol (Yahoo), type (dividend | split | capital_gain), value (per share in the listing currency; split = new shares per old share)
columns.fx.csv: date, usdcad = CAD per 1 USD (USDCAD=X daily close)

hard (symbol excluded): history ends more than 7 days before the window end
missing trading days > 2% of the symbol's own exchange calendar (and more than 3)
soft (symbol kept, warning listed): history starts more than 7 days after the window start
rows with no close price dropped (counted)
qualityChecks.exchangeCalendars: TSX and U.S. calendars are derived from the snapshot itself: a day belongs to an exchange when at least 50% of its symbols live that day have a row. Crypto is expected every calendar day, USD/CAD every weekday.
qualityChecks.neverCorrected: Values are written as Yahoo returned them (rounded to 6 decimals); nothing is filled in.

limitations: Unofficial source: Yahoo Finance data read with yfinance, not certified; yfinance is meant for personal and research use, so this snapshot is for demonstration only, not commercial use.
Survivorship bias: the universe is today's list of large companies, replayed into the past.
No fees and no taxes by default.
Currency effect included: USD assets are converted to CAD at the day's USD/CAD rate.
The window starts in December 2020, close to a market top (2021) before the 2022 decline.
Adjusted closes depend on the extraction date: a new extraction can change past adjusted values, which is why the snapshot is frozen and identified.
